clue.text: Mend garment mostly used in racing competition and play

indicators.note: the mending and the garment are placed inside the racing event, so 'used in' signals a container

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
to mend is to heal

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter, so not all of it is used

parts.note: a chemise is a woman's undergarment

explanation.surface: Someone patches up clothing to be worn at a race meeting and a theatre show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'racing competition' looks like the setting but gives letters; the play is Ben Jonson's 1610 comedy, and 'mostly' drops the garment's final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Jonson's comedy about a con man posing as a transmuter of metals is a famous English stage work.

clue.text: People engaged in wrongful act causing distress

indicators.note: the people are occupied within the wrongful act, so 'engaged in' puts one inside the other

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
men means people

explanation.surface: Some individuals take part in a misdeed that upsets others.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment is severe suffering, a synonym of distress.

clue.text: Royal attendant with energy leading resistance in challenge

indicators.note: in a down clue, the energy symbol leading means it comes before the rest

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: the resistance symbol sits inside the word for challenge

parts.note: to query something is to challenge it
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A palace servant energetically heads the opposition to a challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: An equerry is an officer who personally attends a member of the British royal family.

clue.text: Defamatory statement almost deserved to be released

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: a libel is a written defamatory statement
rated means merited or deserved, as in 'rated a mention'

explanation.surface: A slanderous remark nearly earned someone their freedom.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberated means set free, a synonym of released.

clue.text: Places whose inhabitants are busy and rash

explanation.surface: Busy hubs of activity breaking out in spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Beehives house bustling bees, the proverbially busy insects; hives is also urticaria, an itchy skin rash.

clue.text: Physicist raised stuff about electric current

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word reads upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: to stuff is to cram
on means about or concerning
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A scientist hoisted material around a live wire.
explanation.definitionFit: Guglielmo Marconi was the Italian physicist and inventor who pioneered radio transmission.

clue.text: Do be quiet in tunnel

parts.note: sh is the call to be quiet
to tunnel is to dig

explanation.surface: Keep silent while burrowing underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is a noun here: a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is a lively party, and a do is a social event or celebration.

clue.text: Neat selection possessed by lover of composer with range

indicators.note: the selection is held inside the lover's name, so 'possessed by' signals a container

parts.note: the novelist George Sand was Chopin's lover
a pick is a choice or selection
a span is a range or extent

explanation.surface: A tidy choice owned by a musician's partner, along with a broad scope.
explanation.walkthrough: The composer is Chopin, whose companion was the writer George Sand.
explanation.definitionFit: Spick and span describes something spotlessly clean and tidy, i.e. neat.

clue.text: Upset king surrounded by savage pressure in revolution

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure

indicators.note: turning round in revolution means the letters are read backwards
the king's letter is enclosed by the savage

parts.note: a brute is a savage creature
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch is overthrown by a ferocious mob amid political upheaval.
explanation.walkthrough: R inside BRUTE gives BRUTRE; 'in revolution' turns it to ERTURB, after P.
explanation.definitionFit: To perturb is to disturb or make anxious, a verb matching 'upset'.

clue.text: One with energy after check set about run resulting in giddiness

indicators.note: the one and the energy come after the checking word
the check is placed around the run, so 'set about' signals a container

parts.note: to vet is to check
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
I is the Roman numeral one
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: An energetic person, after an inspection, starts a run that leaves them dizzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertigo is a sensation of spinning dizziness, a synonym of giddiness.

clue.text: Hero injured in attack on particular little community

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it
the jumbled hero goes inside the attack

parts.note: an onset is an attack or assault

indicators.note: an injured hero is damaged, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: own means particular to oneself, as in 'my own'

explanation.surface: A wounded champion assaults a certain small settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'injured' scrambles the hero; in a down clue 'on' puts the attack above the final piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-horse town is a small, dull place with few amenities, i.e. a little community.

clue.text: In course of article are revisions more apparent?

indicators.note: the letters run through the course of the words, so it is a hidden word

explanation.surface: Asking whether revising an article makes it easier to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearer means more obvious or evident, i.e. more apparent.

clue.text: Picture covering mere foot

indicators.note: the picturing word wraps round the mere

parts.note: to picture something is to see it in the mind
a mere is a lake or pond

explanation.surface: An image depicting a simple foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' is a metrical foot in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A spondee is a metrical unit of two stressed syllables in poetry.

clue.text: Article with time put into use in suitable way

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the time letter goes inside the word for use

parts.note: to ply a tool is to use it

explanation.surface: Grammar point and timing applied for a fitting purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Aptly means appropriately, fittingly, in a way that suits.

clue.text: Lecture given by head of state in tense voice

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: the monarch is inside the singing voice

parts.note: alto is a singing voice
a king is a head of state

explanation.surface: A speech delivered by a national leader in a strained voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A talking-to is a reprimand, as is a lecture given to someone who has misbehaved.

clue.text: Large poetical work's sound, attractive thing

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
ode's, an ode being a lyric poem
a tone is a sound

explanation.surface: A long poem has a sound that appeals.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodestone is a naturally magnetised rock, literally a thing that attracts iron.

clue.text: Awful fear admitted by fellow before first bit of dressing's ripped off

indicators.note: the fellow piece comes before the dressing's first letter
the fear is let in by the fellow, so it goes inside

parts.note: a dude is a fellow

indicators.note: awful suggests something messed up, so the letters are rearranged
the first bit means just the opening letter

explanation.surface: A man confesses dreadful fear before his bandage is torn away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' scrambles the fear before it goes inside the fellow; the trailing 's is 'is', linking the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ripped off is to be cheated or swindled.

clue.text: Reject not entirely satisfactory bait

indicators.note: not entirely means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: fair means moderately good, satisfactory
a lure is a bait

explanation.surface: Turning down bait that was not quite good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reject' is a noun: something or someone rejected as no good.
explanation.definitionFit: A failure is a person or thing that does not succeed, a reject.

clue.text: Star, when bearing north, sailor initially espied

indicators.note: to bear is to carry, so the word for when holds the rest

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
a tar is a sailor

indicators.note: initially means the first letter

explanation.surface: A navigator spots a star while heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' looks like a compass heading but is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Antares is the bright red supergiant in Scorpio.

clue.text: Appeal for aid receiving about a thousand items of footwear

indicators.note: the distress call takes in the other letters

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal
c, from circa, means about
K is short for kilo, a thousand

explanation.surface: A charity appeal collects some thousand pairs of shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Socks are garments worn on the feet.

clue.text: Layer formed by acid, rising in quantity

indicators.note: the turned acid word goes inside the quantity

parts.note: a sum is a quantity or amount

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: tart means sharp-tasting, acid

explanation.surface: A coating created by acid building up in volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratum is a layer, especially of rock.

clue.text: Tea followed by expression of happiness or disappointment?

indicators.note: the tea word comes first, then the next piece

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
a grin is a happy facial expression

explanation.surface: Does a cuppa then a smile signal joy or a let-down?
explanation.definitionFit: Chagrin is vexation or annoyance at being disappointed or humiliated.

clue.text: Cutting work back, suggested having hour off?

indicators.note: back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: off means the hour letter is removed

parts.note: hinted means suggested

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone reducing their workload hinted at taking an hour's break.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointed remark is sharp and cutting.

clue.text: Reportedly delivered a letter

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the words are as heard, a homophone

parts.note: dealt a, as in cards delivered to players

explanation.surface: Someone is said to have brought a written message.
explanation.definitionFit: Delta is the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Batman perhaps appointed to impound Joker's latest vehicle

indicators.note: impounding encloses, so the appointed word wraps round the rest

parts.note: set means fixed or appointed, as in a set time

indicators.note: latest means the last letter

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A caped crusader confiscates his comic-book villain's car.
explanation.walkthrough: A batman is a British army officer's personal servant, not the superhero.
explanation.definitionFit: An army officer's batman is his personal attendant, an example of a domestic.

clue.text: Trap soldiers left to secure acceptable objective

indicators.note: the other pieces hold the acceptable letter in place inside

parts.note: a net is a trap
U means upper-class, so socially acceptable
RA is the Royal Artillery

explanation.surface: Ensnaring troops leaves a fair target secured.
explanation.definitionFit: Neutral means impartial, unbiased, i.e. objective.

clue.text: Become too mature for blooming good fight?

parts.note: flowers that are out are in bloom
a row is a quarrel or fight

explanation.surface: Asking whether a flowering, proper scrap is something to leave behind with age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blooming' looks like a mild British swearword but means in flower.
explanation.definitionFit: To outgrow something is to become too old or big for it.

clue.text: Journalist with pen was near MP in tipsy state

indicators.note: drunk letters stagger about, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A reporter with a pen was close to a drunken MP.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaperman is a reporter or journalist who works for a paper.
